title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Array Class
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Array Class - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Introduction of array class".

questions.question: Which class serves as the base class for all arrays in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, every array type is implicitly derived from the 'System.Array' abstract class, which provides methods for creating, manipulating, searching, and sorting arrays.

questions.question: Which interfaces are implemented by the System.Array class?

options.text: All of the mentioned (ICloneable, ICollection, IList, IEnumerable, etc.)

questions.explanation: The Array class implements several key interfaces to support cloning, collections, indexing, and structural comparison/equality.

questions.question: Which statement about the IComparer interface in C# is correct?

options.text: The IComparer interface is located in System.Collections
It defines a Compare(object x, object y) method that returns an integer
Both A and B are correct

questions.explanation: IComparer (non-generic) is in System.Collections. It requires implementing 'Compare(object x, object y)', returning 0 if equal, >0 if x > y, and <0 if x < y.

questions.question: Which statement about the generic IComparer<T> interface is correct?

options.text: It is located in the System.Collections.Generic namespace
It defines the method 'int Compare(T x, T y)'
It provides type safety compared to the non-generic IComparer

questions.explanation: IComparer<T> is the generic version of the comparer interface, allowing for type-safe comparisons of specific types.

questions.question: What is the default behavior of the 'IsReadOnly' property for standard arrays in C#?

options.text: It always returns true because arrays have fixed sizes
It returns true if the array is read-only and false otherwise
It always returns false for standard C# arrays
Both B and C are correct

questions.explanation: The 'IsReadOnly' property is required by the IList interface. For standard C# arrays, it always returns 'false' because the elements can be modified, even though the array size is fixed.

questions.question: What happens if the 'BinarySearch' method does not find the specified value in a sorted array?
questions.code: public static int BinarySearch<T>(T[] array, T value)

options.text: It returns a negative number (the bitwise complement of the next larger element's index)
It returns the length of the array

questions.explanation: If 'BinarySearch' fails to find the element, it returns a negative integer. You can apply the bitwise complement operator (~) to this result to find the index where the element should be inserted to maintain sort order.

questions.explanation: Array.Reverse() reverses the order of the elements in the array. The array {"beta", "alpha", "gamma"} becomes {"gamma", "alpha", "beta"}.

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT way to define and initialize an array of 4 integers?
questions.explanation: Option B is incorrect because it allocates an array of size 3 ('new int[3]') but attempts to assign a value to the 4th element ('a[3]'), which will throw an 'IndexOutOfRangeException'.

questions.question: Which static method of the Array class is used to copy a range of elements from one array to another?
questions.explanation: Array.Copy() is used to copy a range of elements from one array to another, starting at a specified source index and copying to a specified destination index.
